findings.title: The universal string-and-reduction criterion in Proposition 5.6 is false at r=2
findings.claim: Any stable normalized formal genus expansion (5.16) with symmetric positive-index coefficients satisfying H_k^1 Z=nu_k Z for all k>=1 and H_{-r+2}^r Z=mu Z is asserted to equal Z^Theta^r; r=2 is included and no KP/KdV/CohFT hypothesis is stated.

counterexample.Z: (1-t1)^(-1/8) as formal binomial series at zero
counterexample.Phi: Phi_{1,n}[1,...,1]=(n-1)!/8 for n>=1; all others zero
hypotheses_checked: log Z=sum_{n>=1}t1^n/(8n) matches hbar^(g-1)/n! at g=1.
All nonzero terms are stable n>=1 with positive labels, symmetric arrays, and no n=0 term.
Independence of every even time yields H_k^1 Z=0 for every k>=1.
At r=2 the exact shifted operator on even-independent functions is hbar*((1-t1)*d1 - sum_{j>=3 odd} j*t_j*d_j - 1/8), which annihilates Z.
No integrability or CohFT origin is required by the written proposition. The r=2 geometric degree selection also allows this genus-one all-primary sector.

findings.decisive_calculation: Normal ordering leaves only (p1,p2)=(1,1) in H_1^2 Z0. Thus H_1^2 Z0=-(hbar^2/2)*d1^2 Z0=-(9*hbar^2/128)*(1-t1)^(-17/8), nonzero already at all times zero. Theorem 5.5 requires this constraint to vanish for the descendant potential.
findings.proof_failure: At r=2 (5.19) supplies only weight-one modes; it supplies no H_k^2 Z=0 for positive k. The subsequent declaration [H_k^2,H_0^2]Z=0 therefore uses a missing premise. The coefficient k(1-r)-r+2 is -k and vanishes at k=0; merely fixing mu does not repair the example.
findings.core_impact: Proposition 5.18 explicitly invokes the false endpoint criterion and the written r=2 route to Theorem 5.20 invokes Proposition 5.18. The damaged theoretical bridge to a principal conclusion supports Major even though the final equality may have a separate proof.
counterevidence_and_alternative_interpre: This is a normalized stable formal series, not an arbitrary rescaling or unstable input.
H_k^2 is weight two, not an operator square; actual source images and normal ordering were checked.
The proposition contains no r>=3 restriction, KP/KdV premise, or requirement of full W constraints.
The acquired paper states on PDF pages 10 and 63 that full r=2 Virasoro constraints were proved in its references [5,33]; this is a possible independent repair route.
No claim is made that the counterexample is a KP/KdV tau function, that the particular BGW tau function fails a constraint, or that the BGW equality itself is false.
findings.repair_boundary: Exclude r=2 from this universal criterion and supply a separately verified endpoint proof from full Virasoro constraints and Theorem 5.5 uniqueness. No certification of the remaining r>=3 argument or the external replacement proof is made. Normalization, mu=0, the genus expansion, and dimension selection alone are insufficient.

per_problem.independent_reasoning: At r=2 the symmetric genus-one coefficients (n-1)!/8 give log Z=sum t1^n/(8n), which is stable and normalized. Even-time independence gives all H_k^1 Z=0. The stated normally ordered H_0^2 annihilates (1-t1)^(-1/8), while H_1^2=-hbar^2 d1^2/2 gives -9 hbar^2(1-t1)^(-17/8)/128. Thus the complete written premise holds and a required full constraint fails. The root inspected source p.52; the native auxiliary separately inspected pp.48-53 and 62-63 and checked the same operator algebra. Proposition5.6 is used in5.18 and then5.20, establishing a core proof dependency.
per_problem.counterevidence: No KP/KdV/CohFT premise is written in5.6. The particular BGW function is not the counterexample. The source cites previous full r=2 Virasoro results; those may repair the endpoint, but their external proof was not revalidated here.
per_problem.repair_scope: Separate r=2 using independently verified full constraints; no certification of r>=3 or external replacement proof.
